title: Corporate Commons: Operational Policies & Templates
author: Jordan Hale
content:
Overview:

This page consolidates company-wide operational policies and canonical templates for access & permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. It is intended as the single reference for teams to: follow standardized approval flows, reduce cycle time for requests, and ensure consistent compliance with legal/security/finance requirements.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and agents who request or approve changes, access, procurement, vendor onboarding, or travel using company funds or systems.
- Exclusions: specific product-level security controls are documented in Security & Compliance space; this doc focuses on cross-functional process, approvals, and templates.

Key principles:
- Least privilege and separation of duties.
- Clear approval ownership and SLAs.
- Risk-proportionate controls (higher risk -> more reviewers/controls).
- Reuse standardized templates to make audits and reviews efficient.

Governance and roles:
- Policy Owner: Finance & Legal (primary), People Ops (travel/HR overlap), Security (access/data controls).
- Requester: person initiating a change, access, procurement, or vendor onboarding.
- Approver: role required by approval matrix (section below). Approvers must act within SLA.
- Reviewer: optional technical/security reviewer for sensitive requests.
- Audit Owner: Compliance team maintains records for 7 years (unless longer retention required).

Access & Permissions Policy:
Purpose: ensure least-privilege, audited access changes, and periodic reviews.
Principles:
- Default: no broad access groups (e.g., org-wide admin groups are disallowed unless business-justified).
- Access requests must state justification, intended duration, and owner.
- Temporary elevated access must have an expiry and be logged.

Process (step-by-step):
1) Request: submit via Access Request template (see Templates section). Provide justification and requested roles/groups.
2) Manager approval: direct manager approves business need (SLA: 2 business days).
3) Resource owner approval: product/service owner approves technical scope (SLA: 3 business days).
4) Security review: required for requests that access Sensitive/Restricted data (SLA: 5 business days).
5) Fulfillment: IT/Platform performs provisioning and logs the change with ticket reference.
6) Review: quarterly access review by owners; automated reports generated monthly.

Access approval matrix (table - text):
| Request Type | Typical Approvers | Approval Threshold | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Add to dev-only infra group | Manager + Infra Owner | < $0 risk | Standard
| Production credentials (read) | Manager + Service Owner | Low | Logged
| Production credentials (write/admin) | Manager + Service Owner + Security | Elevated | Temporary access recommended
| Data export (sensitive) | Manager + DPO + Security | Elevated | Requires DLP run

Naming & provisioning conventions (short):
- IAM/group names: team-{team-name}-{environment} (e.g. team-data-prod).
- Service accounts: svc-{service-name}-{purpose}.
- All temporary grants use TTL tags and are removed automatically when expired.

Change Management Policy:
Classification:
- Standard Change: routine, pre-authorized, low-risk (examples: patch windows already validated).
- Significant Change: new architecture, infra modifications that affect production SLOs, schema/data migrations. Requires CAB approval.
- Emergency Change: fix to mitigate incidents; must be documented and post-approved.

Change windows and cadence:
- Regular standard change window: weekdays 02:00–04:00 local region for low-impact infra patches.
- Major changes: scheduled with at least 7 business days notice and a rollout plan.
- Emergency changes: allowed outside windows with immediate notification to SRE and postmortem within 72 hours.

Standard change workflow (numbered):
1) Submit Change Request form. Include scope, rollback plan, impact analysis, and runbook.
2) Triage by Change Coordinator within 1 business day.
3) If Significant, route to Change Advisory Board (CAB) with materials 3 business days before scheduled window.
4) Execute per runbook, monitor defined health checks, and verify success.
5) Document outcome and update incident/change logs.

Required artifacts for Significant Changes (checklist):
- Architecture diagram (pre/post).
- Rollback procedure and quick rollback script.
- Performance/load test summary (if applicable).
- Runbook with monitoring playbook and SLOs to observe.

Change approval SLAs:
- Standard: 2 business days.
- Significant: 5 business days to schedule CAB.
- Emergency: post-approval required within 72 hours.

Data Management & Retention:
Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: No confidentiality restrictions.
- INTERNAL: Redwood-internal operational info, allowed company-wide sharing.
- SENSITIVE: Personal data, vendor PII, customer identifiers, or business secrets. Requires encryption at rest and in transit.
- RESTRICTED: Highly sensitive data (e.g., export-controlled, regulated customer PHI/PII). Extra controls and documented legal approvals required.

Retention and deletion rules (table - text):
| Data Type | Classification | Retention Period | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Transaction logs | INTERNAL | 2 years | Platform Engineering |
| Customer PII | SENSITIVE | per contract / default 7 years | Legal & Product |
| Audit logs | RESTRICTED | 7 years | Security/Compliance |
| Marketing collateral | PUBLIC | 0-3 years | Marketing |

Data handling requirements:
- SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED data must be stored only in approved encrypted stores (see Secure Data Location list).
- Masking or anonymization required for analytics work.
- Data exports must be recorded and reviewed by DPO for SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED exports.

Procurement & Expenses:
Purpose: control company spend, ensure contract/PO governance, and streamline reimbursement.
Approval thresholds (approval matrix - text):
| Amount | Approver(s) |
|---:|---|
| Up to $1,000 | Team Manager (expense) / Procurement for POs |
| $1,001–$25,000 | Manager + Finance Approver |
| $25,001–$250,000 | Manager + Finance + Legal review |
| > $250,000 | Exec Sponsor + Legal + Procurement Committee |

Procurement workflow (numbered):
1) Create Purchase Request (PR) using the Purchase Request template: include cost center, justification, vendor, terms.
2) Procurement validates vendor and pricing; Finance assigns budget code.
3) Legal reviews contracts > $25k or containing non-standard terms.
4) PO issued and supplier acknowledged.
5) Supplier onboarding (vendor checklist) completed before payment.

Corporate card and reimbursement rules (high-level):
- Corporate cards provided per role and approved by Finance. Lost cards must be reported within 24 hours.
- Expenses must be submitted within 30 days with receipts; late submissions may be flagged.
- Travel bookings should use preferred vendors/portal unless pre-approved exception.

Vendor Management:
Onboarding checklist (ordered):
1) Complete Vendor Intake Form with scope and business justification.
2) Security review: vendor security questionnaire (VSA) required for third-party access to systems or SENSITIVE data.
3) Legal review: contract terms, liability clause, data protection addendums.
4) Procurement approves pricing/PO terms.
5) Finance sets up vendor profile and payment terms.
6) Operational handoff: owner, escalation contacts, SLAs documented.

Vendor risk categories and controls:
- Low risk: SaaS tools with no access to customer data. Quarterly vendor review.
- Medium risk: vendors processing company internal data; require SOC2 or equivalent and annual review.
- High risk: vendors with access to SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED customer data; require penetration test reports, contractual DPA, and quarterly audits.

Contract & SLA guidance:
- Standard SLA baseline: 99.9% uptime for core infra vendors; defined support response times by severity.
- Include exit and data return/destruction clauses for all contracts handling company data.

Travel & Expense Policy (summary):
Pre-approval:
- All travel must be pre-approved by manager using Travel Request template; include budget code and purpose.
Booking & allowable expenses:
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours; Premium Economy or Business requires Exec pre-approval.
- Hotel: standard business hotels; use preferred vendor rates when available.
- Meals: per diem caps by city (see appendix). Itemized receipts required for reimbursement > $75.
Reimbursement process:
1) Submit Expense Report within 30 days via expense system with receipts and codes.
2) Manager approves within 5 business days.
3) Finance processes reimbursement within the next payroll cycle.

Templates and canonical artifacts (links and filenames):
- Purchase Request Template: templates/purchase-request-2025.md
- Access Request Template: templates/access-request-2025.md
- Change Request & Runbook Template: templates/change-request-runbook-2025.md
- Vendor Intake + Security Questionnaire: templates/vendor-intake-vsa-2025.md
- Travel Request & Expense Template: templates/travel-request-expense-2025.md
- Quarterly Access Review Checklist: templates/access-review-2025.md

Common templates (inline examples):
- Minimal Purchase Request example (YAML):
```
requester: "j.hale@redwood.com"
cost_center: "ENG-PLATFORM"
amount_estimate: "$12,500"
vendor: "Acme Cloud Services"
justification: "Dedicated GPU capacity (Q1 proof-of-concept)"
required_by: "2025-03-01"
approvals: ["manager","finance"]
```

- Access Request example (short form):
Requester: name/email
Resource: service-name-prod
Role: read-only
Justification: support incident X-123
Duration: 72 hours (auto-expire)
Approver: service-owner@example.com

Operator runbooks and monitoring expectations:
- Significant changes must include explicit health-checks: latency < 200ms P50, error rate < 0.1% (during rollout), CPU/GPU utilization thresholds.
- Rollouts should include canary percentage and ramp schedule.

Escalation & exceptions:
- For approvals that exceed SLA, the Change Coordinator or Finance on-call may auto-approve after documented 3 business days with risk note (exception only for low-risk requests).
- All exceptions must be documented and reviewed quarterly by the Governance Committee.

Audit, metrics, and SLAs (operational metrics):
- Access request fulfillment SLA: 3 business days for standard requests.
- Procurement PR to PO SLA: 7 business days for requests < $25k.
- Change approval SLA (significant): 5 business days.
- Quarterly compliance review covering 100% of high-risk vendors and a 10% sample of low/medium vendors.

Appendix: quick reference
- Contacts:
  - Policy Owner (Finance & Legal): finance-legal@redwood.com
  - Change Coordinator: change-coordinator@redwood.com
  - Security Intake: security-intake@redwood.com
  - Procurement: procurement@redwood.com

- Per-diem example (sample):
  - San Francisco: $85/day meals
  - London: £60/day meals
  - Tokyo: ¥5,000/day meals

- Records & retention: all approvals, request forms, and runbooks must be stored in the company Confluence space and backed up to the records archive (retention per table above).

Revision history and maintenance:
- This document is reviewed at least annually by Finance & Legal with input from Security and People Ops. Significant policy changes are published with a 30-day notification window to the company.

Templates directory note:
- Templates referenced above live in the Confluence templates folder (see Templates and keep copies in the Policy archive). When using templates, do not edit master copies; create a copy and fill out the copy.
